findings.title: Materials' 55-point lens gap signals earnings bet
findings.body: Materials trades at a forward P/E of 16.75 versus 35.55 trailing, a 55-point percentile gap — the widest in the table. The market is underwriting 112 percent earnings growth, an aggressive bet that recent margin compression reverses.

findings.title: Health Care's extreme percentile masks modest multiple
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E of 19.99 sits at the 99th percentile of its five-year range, yet the multiple itself is not extreme. The 46 percent compression from trailing suggests analysts expect a massive earnings surge, making the percentile rank a story about expectations, not current cost.

findings.title: Utilities' cheap percentile hides flat growth outlook
findings.body: Utilities' forward P/E of 17.44 is at the 27th percentile, but its trailing multiple is at the 7th — a 20-point gap implying only 8 percent earnings growth. The sector looks cheap on a forward basis, yet the market is not pricing in any meaningful acceleration, leaving the valuation discount intact.
